Your risk increases with age, and people younger than 40 rarely get it. Johns Hopkins notes that early treatment of shingles may prevent PHN, which is why the first 72 hours matter.

en.q: Can you get shingles more than once?
en.a: Yes, although most people have only one episode in their lifetime. The CDC notes that herpes zoster can recur, and Cleveland Clinic adds that repeat episodes are uncommon unless you have a weakened immune system. Adults 50 and older — and adults 19 and older with weakened immune systems — are still recommended to get the two-dose Shingrix vaccine even after having shingles.

en.q: How long does a colonoscopy take from start to finish?
en.a: The exam itself usually takes 30 to 45 minutes — about 15 minutes to guide the scope to the end of the colon and 15 more to inspect the lining on the way out. Plan on about two hours at the hospital or outpatient center to cover check-in, the exam, and 30 to 60 minutes of monitored recovery. Counting the bowel prep that begins several days earlier, the whole process spans a few days.

en.q: How long does it take to recover from a colonoscopy?
en.a: You will spend the first 30 to 60 minutes in recovery before your driver takes you home. Cramping and bloating from the pumped-in air are common in the first hour, and you can eat normally again as soon as you feel ready. You should not drive, operate equipment, or make important decisions until the next day, because the anesthesia takes about 24 hours to wear off completely — NIDDK says most people make a full recovery and return to a normal diet by the next day.

en.q: Do I need someone to drive me home after a colonoscopy?
en.a: Yes. Because you receive sedatives or anesthesia, ASGE says patients are required to have a family member or friend drive them home, and you cannot drive again until the next day. Cleveland Clinic says your driver should expect to wait about two hours altogether, covering your preparation, exam, and recovery.

en.q: Does a colonoscopy take longer if polyps are found?
en.a: Usually only a little. Polyps turn up in about 30% of routine colonoscopies, and removing them on the spot may add another 15 minutes, keeping most exams around 45 minutes — still under the one-hour ceiling NIDDK describes. You will not feel the polyp removal or a biopsy, and the removed tissue goes to a lab, with results back in a few days to weeks.

en.q: How long does an MRI take?
en.a: Most MRI scans take 30 to 60 minutes. Cleveland Clinic says a standard MRI "usually takes 30 to 60 minutes," the NHS gives a usual window of 15 minutes to an hour, and RadiologyInfo.org puts the typical total at 30 to 50 minutes. A cardiac MRI can take up to 90 minutes, and contrast dye adds still more time.

en.q: How long does a brain MRI take with contrast?
en.a: Cleveland Clinic says a brain MRI "can take about 30 minutes to an hour to complete" and that it "may take longer if you're getting a brain MRI with contrast." Plan extra time for placing the IV and the additional image sequences. The NHS also notes you may be asked to wait up to 30 minutes afterward so staff can check for a reaction to the dye.

en.q: Why does an MRI take longer than other scans?
en.a: An MRI collects multiple image runs, or sequences, and RadiologyInfo.org notes that some of them "last several minutes" each. More anatomy or more detail means more sequences, and "the type of exam and the equipment used" also affect total time. If you move too much, UCSF Health warns the images blur and errors result, which stretches your appointment.

en.q: Can I have an MRI if I have a pacemaker or metal implant?
en.a: Usually, but you must be screened first. The NHS asks whether you have metal in your body, such as surgical clips, a pacemaker, or dental fillings or bridges, and RadiologyInfo.org lists implants that need safety evaluation, including some cochlear implants, some brain aneurysm clips, some metal coils in blood vessels, some older defibrillators and pacemakers, and vagal nerve stimulators. Tell your provider and the technologist in advance: the technologist "cannot perform the MRI exam without confirming and documenting the type of implant and MRI compatibility," so an undocumented implant can delay your slot.

en.q: How long does alcohol stay in your blood?
en.a: Alcohol can show up on a blood test for up to about 12 hours after your last drink. Your BAC then falls at an average rate of about 0.016% per hour — roughly one standard drink per hour. A heavy night stretches clearance much longer: a 0.20% BAC takes about 12.5 hours to reach zero.

en.q: How long does alcohol stay in your urine?
en.a: A traditional urine test detects alcohol itself for about 10 to 12 hours. An EtG urine test detects a metabolite of alcohol and can stay positive for 3 to 5 days after drinking. A positive EtG does not mean the person is intoxicated at that moment, and alcohol-containing products like mouthwash or vanilla extract can trigger a positive result.

en.q: Can I drive the morning after drinking?
en.a: Not automatically — alcohol can remain on your breath for 12 to 24 hours, and your body clears only about 0.016% BAC per hour. If you stopped drinking at 2 a.m. with a BAC near 0.20%, you could still be over the limit past midday. Coffee, water, food, and cold showers do not speed this up; only time does. When in doubt, arrange another ride.

en.q: How long can alcohol be detected in a hair test?
en.a: Hair follicle tests can detect alcohol metabolites for up to 90 days. They show drinking patterns over time, not current impairment. For a shorter abstinence window, labs typically use an EtG urine test, which stays positive for 3 to 5 days.

en.q: How long does weed stay in your urine?
en.a: For a standard urine test, THC metabolites are typically detectable for about 3 days after a single use, 5 to 7 days if you use roughly four times per week, 10 to 15 days with daily use, and 30 days or more with multiple uses per day. In chronic users, the inactive metabolite that federally regulated tests screen for can persist for weeks or even months after last use. How often you use is the single biggest factor.

en.q: How long does weed stay in your blood?
en.a: Blood tests mainly catch very recent use, typically within roughly 2 to 12 hours after smoking. In heavy chronic users, though, active THC has been detected in blood about 30 days after the last use. A positive blood result therefore shows past exposure, not proof that you are currently impaired.

en.q: How long does weed stay in your saliva?
en.a: Saliva tests usually detect THC for about 24 hours, and some evidence suggests oral fluid can stay positive for up to about 30 hours after use. In frequent smokers, THC has been detected in oral fluid as long as 72 hours after use. These tests are mainly used to flag recent use, such as in roadside or workplace checks.

en.q: How do I get weed out of my system fast?
en.a: You largely cannot. THC is stored in body fat and clears on its own schedule, so detox kits, gallons of water, and last-minute workouts do not reliably change results — in one study, neither 45 minutes of moderate exercise nor 24 hours of fasting significantly changed blood or urine cannabinoid levels. Stopping as early as possible before the test is the only thing that meaningfully shortens the window.

en.q: How long does a hangover usually last?
en.a: Most hangovers resolve within 24 hours, though the NIAAA notes symptoms can last 24 hours or longer. Severity peaks as your blood alcohol concentration returns to zero, and consensus research documents symptoms as far out as 20 hours after the start of drinking. If you still feel terrible well past a day, dose, sleep loss, and hydration are the usual suspects.

en.q: When does a hangover peak after drinking?
en.a: Hangover symptoms peak when your blood alcohol concentration returns to about zero — for a typical evening session, that means the worst hits the next morning, not while you are still drinking. Both NIAAA and the Alcohol Hangover Research Group describe this zero-BAC peak. Counterintuitively, you feel worst after the alcohol itself is gone.

en.q: Is there a cure that makes a hangover go away faster?
en.a: No. A BMJ review of randomized controlled trials found no compelling evidence that any conventional or complementary intervention prevents or treats hangover, and NIAAA states there is no cure other than time. Coffee only masks sleepiness, and a morning drink can prolong the malaise. Water, food, rest, and careful painkiller use can ease the wait.

en.q: Why do some hangovers last longer than others?
en.a: Dose is the biggest factor: in general, the more alcohol you drink, the worse and longer the hangover. Drink type matters too — in a controlled trial, bourbon drinkers felt significantly worse than vodka drinkers at the same breath alcohol level because bourbon is congener-heavy. Broken sleep and individual biology also play a role; women tend to have more severe, longer hangovers than men.

en.q: How long does a tattoo take to heal?
en.a: The visible outer layer of skin usually looks healed in 2 to 3 weeks, and Mayo Clinic says most tattoos take about two weeks. Underneath, Cleveland Clinic says the top layer of skin should be healed by the two-month mark, while the deeper layers take several more months. Healthline notes the full healing process beneath the surface can take up to 12 months.

en.q: How often should I wash and moisturize my new tattoo?
en.a: Wash the tattoo twice a day with a mild, fragrance-free, antibacterial soap and warm — not hot — water, then pat it dry with a clean paper towel. Follow with a water-based moisturizer or artist-recommended ointment twice a day, or several times a day for the first two to three weeks. Consistent cleaning and moisturizing helps prevent scabbing, cracking, and scarring.

en.q: When can I go swimming after getting a tattoo?
en.a: Not until the tattoo is fully healed — stay out of pools, hot tubs, bathtubs, rivers, and lakes. A healing tattoo is an open wound, and soaking it exposes that wound to bacteria. Since deep healing can continue for months, treat swimming as off-limits at least until the skin is completely smooth and every scab has fallen off.

en.q: How do I know if my tattoo is infected?
en.a: See a doctor if you notice fever or chills, skin that feels hot to the touch, odor or significant drainage, pain that keeps getting worse, or red streaks spreading from the tattoo toward the center of your body. Fluid or pus oozing from the tattoo, or swelling, discoloration, and itchiness that will not go away, are also warning signs. Mayo Clinic advises contacting a healthcare professional right away rather than waiting it out.

en.q: What is the best time to post on Instagram right now?
en.a: There is no single magic hour — the biggest 2026 studies openly disagree. Sprout Social's analysis of nearly 2 billion engagements points to midweek afternoons, especially Tuesday 1–7 PM and Wednesday 12–9 PM; Hootsuite favors late afternoons plus a Tuesday 5–8 AM window; Later's overall winner is 5 AM. All of these are your audience's local time, and Tuesday through Thursday is the safest block to start testing.

en.q: What is the worst time to post on Instagram?
en.a: In Sprout Social's 2026 data, Saturdays draw the lowest engagement of the week and Sundays are close behind, so the weekend is the weakest slot for an important post. Sprout also flags early mornings from 3 to 7 AM as a dead zone, and Later's worst specific slots were Thursday 3 AM and Saturday 11 PM. Note the exception, though: Later found posts between 3 AM and 6 AM actually earn higher-than-average engagement, which is exactly why your own data should have the final word.

en.q: Do time zones change the best time to post on Instagram?
en.a: Yes — all the major studies publish their recommendations in your audience's local time, not yours. Hootsuite localized its analysis across 118 countries, and Sprout Social says to schedule for your followers' local hours whether they sit in Los Angeles or London. If your audience spans regions, target the overlap between zones or alternate posts between them.

en.q: How do I find my own best time to post on Instagram?
en.a: Open Instagram Insights on a professional account, go to Total Followers, and study the "Most active times" heatmap for each day of the week. Cross-reference that chart with the day and hour of your ten best-performing recent posts, then rotate similar content across two or three candidate windows for two to four weeks, comparing reach and saves rather than likes. Buffer recommends rechecking your best times every few months, since optimal windows drift as your audience grows.

en.q: What is the best time to post on TikTok?
en.a: Sprout Social's 2026 analysis of nearly 2 billion engagements puts it at Tuesday through Friday, 2–6 p.m. in your audience's local time. Buffer's study of 7.1 million posts leans the other way, with engagement peaking in the 6–11 p.m. evening hours and Sunday 9 a.m. standing as the single best slot of the week. Treat both as starting points and confirm them against your own TikTok analytics.

en.q: What are the best times to post on TikTok each day of the week?
en.a: By Buffer's 2026 data: Monday 1 p.m., Tuesday 6 a.m., Wednesday 10 p.m., Thursday 1 p.m., Friday 6 p.m., Saturday 5 p.m., and Sunday 9 a.m., which was the strongest slot of the entire week. Sprout Social instead favors weekday afternoons such as Tuesday–Friday 2–6 p.m. and calls weekends the weakest days. Let your own followers' active hours break the tie between the two datasets.

en.q: How often should you post on TikTok?
en.a: Buffer's analysis of 11.4 million TikTok posts found that 2–5 posts per week is the sweet spot, bringing up to 17 percent more views per post than posting once a week; heavier schedules reach up to 29–34 percent more but with diminishing returns per extra post. TikTok itself recommends posting 1–4 times per day, according to Hootsuite. Whatever cadence you choose, watch time still decides how far each video travels.

en.q: Does the time you post on TikTok really matter?
en.a: Yes, but less than most creators assume. Posting when your followers are online helps a video win its first small test audience, which can trigger wider distribution on the For You feed. TikTok says it gives the greatest weight to strong interest signals like a viewer finishing a video, and that follower count is not a direct ranking factor, so watch time and hook quality matter more than any posting window. In Buffer's phrasing, timing is a boost, not a fix.

en.q: How long does a wheel alignment take?
en.a: Plan on about an hour of bay time. Les Schwab says a wheel alignment can take up to one hour once your vehicle is in the service bay, and GoodCar puts most alignments at approximately 60 minutes. Your total visit runs longer once you add waiting-room time and any repairs the technician finds.

en.q: Does a four-wheel alignment take longer than a two-wheel alignment?
en.a: Usually not. According to GoodCar, a four-wheel alignment takes about the same amount of time as any other alignment — roughly 60 minutes — as long as there are no suspension or steering issues. What differs is price: J.D. Power puts a front-end (two-wheel) alignment at $50 to $75 and a four-wheel alignment at $100 to $168.

en.q: Why would a wheel alignment take longer than an hour?
en.a: The biggest factors are a severe misalignment and worn or bent suspension or steering parts discovered mid-job, which must be repaired before the car can be aligned. Luxury vehicles that require specialized equipment and models with rear steering, stability control, or Steering Angle Sensors also add steps, according to J.D. Power and Firestone.

en.q: How often should you get a wheel alignment?
en.a: Firestone recommends an alignment check every 6,000 miles or 6 months — about every other oil change — while Les Schwab suggests at least once a year, and ideally twice. Also get the alignment checked right after a hard pothole or curb impact, or whenever you buy new tires.

en.q: How long does it take cucumbers to turn into pickles?
en.a: It depends on how sour you want them. Half-sour dills finish in 4 to 6 days at 60 to 77°F, while full-sours take about 3 to 4 weeks at 70 to 75°F, or 5 to 6 weeks in a cooler 55 to 65°F spot. Refrigerator dills are fermented for about 1 week. Taste is the real timer: refrigerate the jar when the sourness suits you.

en.q: How do you know when fermented pickles are done?
en.a: Taste one — pull a pickle around day 4, then every day or two until the sourness and texture please you. Cloudy brine, white sediment, and rising bubbles are all signs of normal fermentation, and the NCHFP considers fermentation complete when bubbling ceases. But if pickles become soft, slimy, or develop a disagreeable odor, discard them — that is spoilage, not extra fermentation.

en.q: What temperature is best for fermenting pickles?
en.a: 70 to 75°F is the target: the NCHFP calls it the optimum temperature for the organisms that drive fermentation, and classic dills finish in about 3 to 4 weeks there. Temperatures of 55 to 65°F are acceptable but slow the ferment to 5 to 6 weeks. Avoid temperatures above 80°F, or the pickles will become too soft during fermentation.

en.q: Do fermented pickles need to be refrigerated after fermentation?
en.a: Yes, unless you can them. Refrigerating the jar stops additional souring and holds the pickles at the flavor you chose; fully fermented pickles keep about 4 to 6 months in the refrigerator in their original container, provided surface scum and molds are removed regularly. For shelf-stable storage, the NCHFP says canning is the better route — 10 minutes for pints and 15 for quarts at elevations up to 1,000 ft.

en.q: How long do flies live inside your house?
en.a: An adult house fly typically lives 15 to 25 days — males about 15 days and females up to 25. In the wild, most house flies survive less than one month. The exact lifespan depends on temperature, food availability, and predators.

en.q: Do flies really die after 24 hours?
en.a: No — Terminix pest experts explicitly call this a common myth. House fly adults normally live two to four weeks, not a single day. Flies in your kitchen are usually adults with most of that lifespan still ahead of them.

en.q: How long is a fly's life cycle from egg to adult?
en.a: Under optimal summer conditions a house fly can go from egg to adult in as little as 7 days, typically 7 to 10. Eggs hatch in 12 to 24 hours in warm weather, and the pupal stage takes just 2 to 6 days at 35°C. In cold or adverse conditions the whole cycle can stretch to about two months.

en.q: How long do fruit flies and horse flies live?
en.a: Fruit fly adults can live up to 30 days, and their full life cycle lasts 25 days or more — though they can complete development in as little as a week in ideal warmth. Horse flies are far slower: most species produce one generation per year, and some take two to three years to finish developing.

en.q: How long is a soccer game in total?
en.a: On the clock, a soccer game is 90 minutes — two 45-minute halves — but stoppage time stretches the average professional match to 100 minutes and 36 seconds of match time in the Premier League this season. Once you add the halftime interval of up to 15 minutes, a normal game runs about 1 hour 55 minutes to 2 hours from kick-off to the final whistle.

en.q: How long is a soccer game with halftime?
en.a: Halftime can last no more than 15 minutes under Law 7 of the Laws of the Game, and competition rules must state the exact length. With a 45-minute first half plus a few minutes of stoppage time, the second half usually kicks off about an hour after the opening whistle, putting the whole match at roughly 1 hour 55 minutes to 2 hours.

en.q: How long is a high school or youth soccer game?
en.a: High school games under NFHS rules are played as two 40-minute halves, for 80 minutes of playing time. Youth games step down by age under US Youth Soccer rules, from two 45-minute halves at 17U-19U to four 6-minute quarters — just 24 minutes of play — at 6U.

en.q: How long does a soccer game last with extra time and penalties?
en.a: Knockout matches that are level after 90 minutes go to two extra-time periods of up to 15 minutes each, under Law 10 of the Laws of the Game. If the score is still tied, a penalty shootout follows — five kicks per team, then sudden death — so a deciding game can stretch close to two and a half hours, and sometimes beyond, from kick-off to the winning kick.

en.q: How long is the average MLB game?
en.a: The average nine-inning MLB game lasted 2 hours 38 minutes in 2025, the most recent full season. That is up just 2 minutes from 2024 but down 26 minutes from 3:04 in 2022, the last season before the pitch timer. Plan on roughly two and a half to three hours from first pitch to final out.

en.q: How long should I plan to be at a baseball game?
en.a: Budget about 2 hours 40 minutes for a typical game, then pad by 30-45 minutes for the two things that break the model: extra innings and rain delays. A 7:05 p.m. start at league-average pace ends around 9:45 p.m., with late extras pushing past 10:15. Postseason games run longer, thanks to 2:55 between-inning breaks and more pitching changes.

en.q: What happens if a baseball game is tied after 9 innings?
en.a: The game keeps going — baseball has no clock to expire, so extra innings are open-ended. In the regular season, every half-inning beyond the ninth starts with an automatic runner on second base (the ghost runner), a rule made permanent in 2023 that usually settles games quickly. The ghost runner is not used in the postseason, so October extras can turn into marathons.

en.q: Why did MLB games get shorter in 2023?
en.a: MLB introduced a pitch timer in 2023: 15 seconds between pitches with the bases empty and 20 with runners on, trimmed to 18 seconds for 2024, plus a 30-second timer between batters. Violations cost an automatic ball or strike. The average game dropped 24 minutes, from 3:04 in 2022 to 2:40 in 2023, and has stayed in the 2:36-2:38 range since.

en.q: How long is halftime in an NFL game?
en.a: NFL halftime is 13 minutes long, set by Rule 4, Section 1, Article 3 of the NFL rulebook, and the Back Judge times it on the field. The same 13-minute intermission applies to regular-season and playoff games. In practice, the second half reliably starts less than 15 minutes after the first half ends.

en.q: How long is Super Bowl halftime?
en.a: The Super Bowl break typically lasts 25 to 30 minutes, roughly twice a normal week, because crews need time to build and tear down the concert stage without damaging the field. The halftime show itself runs about 12 to 14 minutes inside that longer break. With kickoff at 6:30 p.m. ET, halftime usually begins between 8:00 and 8:15 p.m. ET.

en.q: Why is NFL halftime shorter than college football halftime?
en.a: NCAA halftimes last 20 minutes by rule, a full seven minutes longer than the NFL's 13-minute intermission. The NFL cut its break from 15 minutes to 12 in 1990 and lists it at 13 today, keeping the broadcast window tight. That is why a Saturday college game can drift at the midpoint while an NFL game snaps back into action.

en.q: What do NFL players and coaches actually do at halftime?
en.a: Thirteen minutes is barely enough time to get off the field and back. Then-Saints coach Sean Payton said in 2013 that halftime is mostly “getting something to drink, going to the bathroom” while coaches talk through a few adjustments. Coaches can shift overall strategy, but there is little time to meet with individual position groups.

en.q: How long is an NBA game in real time?
en.a: An NBA game is 48 minutes of playing time — four 12-minute quarters — but the rulebook wraps that in a 15-minute halftime, 2:30 quarter breaks and mandatory TV timeouts. Commissioner Adam Silver put the average regular-season game at about 2 hours 15 minutes from tip-off to the final buzzer, so budget two and a quarter hours, plus more if there is overtime.

en.q: How long is a college basketball game?
en.a: Men's college games are two 20-minute halves and women's games are four 10-minute quarters — 40 minutes of clock either way — with a 15-minute halftime and 5-minute overtime periods. Media timeouts, fouls and official reviews stretch the broadcast well beyond the 40 minutes of playing time.

en.q: How long is a high school basketball game?
en.a: Under NFHS rules, high school games are four 8-minute quarters, or 32 minutes of playing time. Teams get 1-minute breaks after the first and third quarters and a 10-minute halftime that can be extended to 15 minutes for special activities, and overtime periods run 4 minutes each.

en.q: What was the longest basketball game ever played?
en.a: The longest Division I men's game on record is Cincinnati's 75-73 seven-overtime win over Bradley on December 21, 1981 — 75 minutes of playing time, 35 of them after regulation. NBA, college and FIBA overtimes are all 5 minutes, and extra periods simply repeat until someone wins.

en.q: How long is an NHL game in real time?
en.a: An NHL game has 60 minutes of playing time, but from puck drop to final horn it typically runs about two and a half hours. A 7:00 p.m. start usually ends around 9:30 p.m., and a game decided in overtime and a shootout pushes closer to 9:45. Whistles, reviews and television timeouts are what stretch the clock.

en.q: How long are intermissions at an NHL game?
en.a: NHL intermissions are 18 minutes each, two per game, and the clock starts the moment the last official leaves the ice (Rules 77.2 and 34.2). That builds 36 minutes into your evening for the zamboni to resurface the ice. College hockey uses 12- or 15-minute breaks and IIHF or Olympic games use 15-minute breaks.

en.q: How does NHL overtime work, and how much time does it add?
en.a: In the regular season, a tied game goes to five minutes of 3-on-3 sudden-death overtime that the rulebook expects to start roughly two minutes after regulation ends. If nobody scores, a three-round-per-team shootout decides it, and those games typically finish about two hours 45 minutes after puck drop. In the playoffs there is no shootout: teams take a 15-minute intermission and then play 20-minute sudden-death periods, repeating until someone scores.

en.q: Is a college or Olympic hockey game shorter than an NHL game?
en.a: Not much — every level plays three 20-minute periods, so the evening is similar at about two and a half hours. College games actually run a bit shorter thanks to 12- or 15-minute intermissions, and the men's game now uses five minutes of 3-on-3 overtime plus a mandatory three-player shootout (women's games can still end tied unless conference policy adds a shootout). Olympic and IIHF games use 15-minute intermissions with five- or ten-minute overtimes plus a shootout, and repeated sudden-death periods in gold-medal games.

en.q: How long is the Super Bowl halftime show itself?
en.a: The musical performance itself runs about 12 to 14 minutes. Kendrick Lamar's 2025 set lasted 13 minutes 20 seconds, and Rihanna fit 13 songs into roughly 13 minutes in 2023. There is no rulebook length for the show — the runtime is a production decision by the artist, the league, and the network.

en.q: How long is the full halftime break at the Super Bowl?
en.a: The entire break lasts 25 to 30 minutes, roughly double a regular-season halftime. A normal NFL halftime is 13 minutes by rule (Rule 4, Section 1, Article 3) and is timed by the Back Judge. The Super Bowl stretches it to fit the stage build, commercials, and studio analysis around the performance.

en.q: What time does the Super Bowl halftime show start?
en.a: With kickoffs around 6:30 p.m. ET and first halves that run about 75 minutes of real time, the first note usually lands between 8:00 and 8:30 p.m. ET. Sporting News projected about 8:00 p.m. for the 2025 show, but the 2024 show did not begin until 8:25 p.m. ET. If you are tuning in just for the music, be watching by about 7:45 p.m. ET.

en.q: Why is Super Bowl halftime longer than a regular-season halftime?
en.a: The rulebook mandates just a 13-minute intermission, but the Super Bowl deliberately doubles it to 25 to 30 minutes. A crew needs roughly six minutes to assemble the stage on the field, and the network fills the rest of the break with the most expensive commercials of the TV year plus studio commentary. That extended break is a big reason the broadcast runs three and a half to four hours.

en.q: How long does an NFL game actually last?
en.a: An NFL game has 60 minutes of playing time, but the average broadcast runs about 3 hours and 12 minutes from kickoff to the final whistle. Only roughly 18 minutes of that is live action, while commercials fill about 45 minutes. Plan on a three-hour commitment with a little slack.

en.q: How long is halftime in an NFL game?
en.a: By NFL rule, halftime is a 13-minute intermission timed by the back judge. The break you experience at home feels longer because networks wrap studio coverage around it. The Super Bowl is the exception: stage setup and teardown stretch its halftime closer to 25-30 minutes.

en.q: How long are college and high school football games?
en.a: College games have the same 60 minutes of playing time as the NFL but average about 3 hours 24 minutes, because they run roughly 40 more plays and allow halftimes up to 20 minutes. High school games are shorter on the clock — 48 minutes in four 12-minute quarters — so their real-time length varies by state.

en.q: How long is NFL overtime?
en.a: In the regular season, overtime is a single 10-minute period, and the game ends in a tie if the score is still level after it. In the postseason, overtime periods run 15 minutes and keep repeating until a winner is decided. In both formats, each team gets an opportunity to possess the ball.

en.q: How long is halftime in the NBA?
en.a: NBA halftime is 15 minutes long in every game, from opening night to Game 7 of the Finals. The figure is fixed by the NBA rulebook (Rule No. 5, Section II—Timing): "Fifteen minutes will be permitted between halves of all games." Television pads the break with studio segments and commercials, but the arena's 15-minute clock is the official number.

en.q: Is NBA halftime longer in the playoffs or the Finals?
en.a: No — the same 15-minute interval is written into the rules for all games, and the league publishes no separate playoff number. Special halftime performances can push the real break toward 20 or 30 minutes on showcase nights, and playoff broadcasts overall run roughly 12 to 13 minutes longer than regular-season games. But the halftime clock itself never changes.

en.q: How long are the breaks between quarters in the NBA?
en.a: By rule, the break between the first-and-second and third-and-fourth quarters is 2:30 in locally televised games and 3:30 when the game airs on national TV. Before any overtime period, 2:30 is permitted. Those between-quarter pauses are far shorter than the 15-minute halftime.

en.q: How long does a full NBA game last including halftime?
en.a: An average regular-season game that ends in regulation ran about 2 hours 13 minutes in 2021-22, and every season from 2016-17 through 2021-22 landed between 2:12 and 2:14, per The Hoops Geek's game data. One overtime pushes the average to about 2:35. That total includes the 15-minute halftime, the quarter breaks and all timeouts.

en.q: How long is a quarter in an NFL game?
en.a: An NFL quarter is 15 minutes of game-clock time, and the rulebook sets the full game at 60 minutes across four periods. Because the clock stops for incomplete passes, penalties, scoring plays, and TV breaks, a real NFL quarter usually takes about 40 to 45 minutes of wall-clock time. Four quarters plus a 13-minute halftime is why the average NFL game runs just over three hours.

en.q: How long is a quarter in high school football?
en.a: High school quarters are 12 minutes long under NFHS-based rules used in most states, for 48 minutes of total playing time; Texas plays under NCAA-based rules but also uses the 12-minute quarter. That is three minutes less per quarter than the NFL, NCAA, and CFL. It is the main reason Friday-night games finish so much earlier than Saturday and Sunday broadcasts.

en.q: How many minutes does a football quarter take in real time?
en.a: Budget roughly 40 to 50 minutes of real time per quarter. An NFL quarter averages about 40 to 45 minutes once stoppages are counted, while a college quarter runs closer to 45 to 50 minutes because of longer halftimes and a heavier commercial load — the average 2024 college game lasted 3 hours, 27 minutes. Treat every quarter as roughly three times its official length and you can predict a game's finish within about ten minutes.

en.q: How long is halftime between the second and third quarter?
en.a: An NFL halftime is 13 minutes between the second and third periods. A college halftime is 20 minutes in the regular season, unless both schools agree before kickoff to shorten it, and in the CFL the second half kicks off exactly 16 minutes after the first half ends. The Super Bowl is the exception — its halftime runs far longer to fit the halftime show.

en.q: How long does the average tennis match last?
en.a: A typical professional best-of-three match lasts about 90 minutes — around 1 hour 20 minutes if it ends in straight sets and about 2 hours if it goes three. Men's Grand Slam matches, which are best-of-five, average about 2 hours 45 minutes, with a typical range of 2 hours to 3 hours 20 minutes.

en.q: What was the longest tennis match ever played?
en.a: John Isner's 2010 Wimbledon first-round win over Nicolas Mahut lasted 11 hours and 5 minutes spread across three days, June 22-24, finishing 70-68 in the fifth set with a record 183 games. The deciding set alone ran 8 hours 11 minutes. Since 2022, a 10-point tiebreak at 6-6 in final sets has made a repeat impossible at the Grand Slams.

en.q: How long is a women's tennis match compared to a men's match?
en.a: Women's matches are best-of-three at every event, including the Grand Slams, so they average about 90 minutes. Men's matches are also best-of-three at regular tour events, but best-of-five at the four majors, which pushes the average up to about 2 hours 45 minutes and creates the famous marathon fifth sets.

en.q: Is there a time limit or shot clock in tennis?
en.a: There is no game clock — a match ends when a player wins the required number of sets, whether that takes 30 minutes or all day. The only between-point timing rule is the ITF's 25-second serve-clock standard, which keeps play moving but cannot shorten the rallies themselves. Since March 2022, final sets at the Grand Slams also end in a 10-point tiebreak at 6-6, which caps how long a deciding set can run.

en.q: How long does it take the average person to run a marathon?
en.a: The average finisher worldwide covers the 26.2 miles in about 4:30 — RunRepeat's study of 107.9 million results put the 2018 global average at 4:32:49. Men average close to 4:21 and women close to 4:51, with the fastest age band (30 to 50) averaging about 4:24.

en.q: What is the fastest marathon time ever run?
en.a: The men's world record is 1:59:30, set by Sabastian Sawe at the 2026 London Marathon — the first sub-two-hour marathon in record-eligible race conditions. Ruth Chepngetich holds the women's mixed-race record at 2:09:56 (Chicago 2024), and Tigst Assefa set the women-only record of 2:15:41 at the 2026 London Marathon.

en.q: How long do you have to finish a marathon before the course closes?
en.a: It depends on the race. The Chicago Marathon keeps its course open for 6 hours 30 minutes — roughly a 15:00 per mile pace — and warns that runners finishing after 4 p.m. may not be recorded as official finishers. Most big-city marathons stay open six and a half hours or more, so always check your specific race's published cutoff.

en.q: What pace do you need to qualify for the Boston Marathon?
en.a: For the 2027 race, men aged 18–34 must have run 2:55:00 or faster — about 6:41 per mile — and women 3:25:00. Standards step up by age group all the way to 4:50:00 for men and 5:20:00 for women aged 80 and over, and hitting the standard only qualifies you to apply for entry.

en.q: How long is a 12-round boxing match?
en.a: A full 12-round championship fight contains 36 minutes of actual boxing — twelve 3-minute rounds — plus eleven 1-minute rest periods, which works out to about 47 minutes from the first bell to the final bell. Add ring walks, introductions and the decision, and the main event fills roughly an hour of broadcast. If it ends early by knockout or stoppage, it can be over in minutes.

en.q: How long is an Olympic boxing match?
en.a: Olympic and elite amateur bouts are three rounds of 3 minutes with 1-minute breaks between them, the same format for men and women. That is just 9 minutes of actual boxing and roughly 11 minutes bell to bell, far shorter than a professional title fight.

en.q: How long are women's boxing matches?
en.a: Women's championship bouts are contested over 10 rounds of 2 minutes each — 20 minutes of fighting, about 29 minutes bell to bell. That is a minute less per round and two rounds fewer than the men's 12 x 3-minute championship format, and the debate over switching women to three-minute rounds is ongoing. A full women's title fight actually contains less fighting time than an 8-round men's bout.

en.q: How long does a boxing fight night last on TV?
en.a: The main event alone runs about an hour with ring walks and the decision, but a televised card stacks several undercard bouts in front of it. A five-bout card with 4-, 6-, 8- and 10-round support fights ahead of a 12-round main event carries 155 minutes of scheduled ring time alone, before any television padding. Expect the full broadcast to run three hours or more unless a run of early knockouts shortens the night.

en.q: How many hours does a NASCAR race last?
en.a: Most NASCAR Cup Series races run about three hours from green flag to checkered flag. Recent official times range from 2:48:03 for a 300-mile race to 4:25:08 for the Coca-Cola 600, and those figures exclude red-flag stoppages, so a rain-hit race can occupy far more of your day.

en.q: How long does the Daytona 500 take to run?
en.a: The Daytona 500 is scheduled for 200 laps, or 500 miles, and usually finishes in three to three and a half hours. It ran 3:10:52 in 2024, 3:53:26 in 2025 (eight cautions, plus rain red flags that added over three and a half hours of waiting), and 3:23:56 in 2026.

en.q: How long is the Coca-Cola 600?
en.a: The Coca-Cola 600 at Charlotte Motor Speedway is NASCAR's longest race: 400 laps and 600 miles on Memorial Day weekend. The 2025 edition, won by Ross Chastain, took 4:25:08 with eight cautions, so plan for at least a four-and-a-half-hour window.

en.q: Why do some NASCAR races take longer than others?
en.a: Race length is set by a fixed distance, not a clock, so cautions do most of the damage — the Daytona 500 ran 3:10 with five cautions in 2024 but 3:53 with eight in 2025. Every race also includes two scheduled stage-break cautions, rain can red-flag it for hours, and an overtime finish can add laps beyond the scheduled distance, as when Martinsville's 400-lap race became 415 laps in 2024.

en.q: How long does it take for eyebrows to grow back after plucking?
en.a: Plan on the first new hairs at about 2 to 3 months, because the full eyebrow growth cycle runs 3 to 4 months. Complete fill-in can take up to 6 months. If nothing has changed after 4 months, Cleveland Clinic says it is time to see a dermatologist.

en.q: Do eyebrows grow back after shaving them off?
en.a: Yes. In a small 1999 study, five people fully shaved off one eyebrow and every one of them had complete regrowth by 6 months. Shaving cuts the hair at the skin surface without damaging the follicle, which makes it far less risky for regrowth than daily plucking.

en.q: Will overplucked eyebrows grow back after years of plucking?
en.a: Usually, as long as the follicles are not scarred — "most of the time, they grow back," says Cleveland Clinic dermatologist Dr. Shilpi Khetarpal. But plucking every day can cause scarring, and scarred follicles may never produce hair again. Stop plucking completely, wait a full 4 months, and see a dermatologist if nothing grows.

en.q: How can I make my eyebrows grow back faster?
en.a: Stop plucking and toss the magnifying mirror so the follicles can recover. Cleveland Clinic suggests 3 to 5 milligrams of biotin daily (plus iron or omega-3s if you rarely eat red meat or fish), and 2% or 5% minoxidil can help — just keep it out of your eyes. Give any routine a full 4 months, one complete growth cycle, before judging results.

en.q: How long does it take for eyelashes to grow back?
en.a: Most eyelashes grow back in about 6 weeks if the follicle is undamaged — the same timeline whether the lash fell out, was pulled, or was cut or singed. One complete growth cycle, from a new lash emerging to it shedding, takes 4 to 11 months. If a gap shows no new short stubble after a couple of months, see a dermatologist or ophthalmologist.

en.q: Do eyelashes grow back after eyelash extensions?
en.a: Yes — lashes shed when extensions are removed typically regrow in about 6 weeks if the follicle is intact. The bigger risk is the extensions and glue themselves, which can injure follicles and cause temporary or even permanent damage. Giving your lashes a break helps quickly: in a 2024 study, dry-eye comfort and tear quality improved within four weeks of removal.

en.q: Can you make eyelashes grow back faster?
en.a: You cannot speed up the growth cycle itself — the most effective move is removing the cause: stop pulling, tugging, and gluing. The only FDA-approved lash-growth medication is prescription bimatoprost 0.03% (Latisse), approved in 2008; in a randomized trial, 78.1% of users improved by at least one grade at week 16 versus 18.4% on vehicle. Castor oil and other over-the-counter options mainly condition lashes rather than regrow them.

en.q: Why won't my eyelashes grow back?
en.a: The most common reason is follicle damage from scarring, repeated pulling, or extension glue — a scarred follicle will not regrow a lash on its own. Underlying conditions can also be at work: blepharitis, alopecia areata, thyroid disorders, and stress-related telogen effluvium all thin lashes. If a patch has no new stubble after a couple of months, or the lash line is red, scaly, or itchy, see a dermatologist or ophthalmologist.

en.q: How long does a perm last on average?
en.a: Most perms last three to six months — the same window given by Healthline, WebMD, and Hair Professionals Career College. Root perms fade in a few weeks, and straightening perms hold for around three months. The curl itself is permanent; what ends the style is new straight hair growing in at roughly 1 cm per month.

en.q: How long after getting a perm can I wash my hair?
en.a: Wait at least 48 hours before shampooing, and keep hair dry and relatively untouched while the bonds set. Hair Professionals Career College also advises not combing at all for the first 24 hours. After the first wash, detangle with a wide-tooth comb or your fingers instead of a brush.

en.q: How often should you get a perm redone?
en.a: Most people re-perm every 3 to 4 months, in line with WebMD's note that a touch-up at month 3 may be safe. By then about 3 cm of straight regrowth has flattened the roots and the ends have relaxed into waves. WebMD cautions that perms are riskiest on hair that is already overly processed or damaged, so previously treated lengths need a lighter touch.

en.q: How can I make my perm last longer?
en.a: Keep hair dry and untouched for the first 48 hours, and avoid coloring for two weeks before and after the appointment — waiting at least a month after perming to dye, per Healthline. Skip chlorine, heat styling, and alcohol-based products, and use leave-in conditioner and protein treatments as WebMD recommends. Sleep on your stomach or side or under a silk cap, wear a wide-brimmed hat in the sun, and trim every 6–8 weeks.

en.q: How much does hair grow in a month?
en.a: Scalp hair grows about 1 centimeter (0.4 inches) per month, according to the Cleveland Clinic. That adds up to roughly 12 centimeters, or about 4.7 inches, in a year. Your personal rate can be higher or lower — a study of 2,249 adults from 24 ethnic groups found growth differs by origin, scalp area, and gender.

en.q: How long does it take for hair to grow 1 inch?
en.a: At the average pace of about 1 centimeter a month, hair needs roughly two and a half months to add a full inch. That is why dermatology sources suggest judging progress in three-month blocks rather than week to week — a month of growth is usually too little to see clearly in the mirror.

en.q: Does trimming your hair make it grow faster?
en.a: No. Growth begins at the root — the dermal papilla inside the follicle, which supplies blood and nutrients — so cutting the ends cannot affect the rate. Trims do help by stopping split ends from traveling up the shaft, which protects the length you already have.

en.q: Why does it look like my hair stopped growing?
en.a: Usually it is breakage, not slow follicles: tension from tight styles, brushing wet hair, and heat styling erase the millimeters you grew, so the mirror shows no progress. There is also a genetic ceiling — anagen lasts 2 to 7 years, and your maximum length is roughly 1 centimeter a month multiplied by that phase. If you are also shedding heavily more than two months after a stressful event, that is usually temporary telogen effluvium; see a dermatologist if it passes six months.

en.q: How long does it take for a fingernail to grow back?
en.a: A fingernail that is entirely removed takes 6 months or longer to grow back, according to the AAD, and the NHS says a fingernail lost to injury should regrow within about 6 months. Fingernails only grow about 3.47 mm per month — roughly a centimeter every three months — so even a stain or bruise in an intact nail takes months to travel to the tip and be trimmed off.

en.q: How long does it take for a toenail to grow back?
en.a: About 12 to 18 months. Toenails grow just 1.62 mm per month on average, less than half the fingernail rate, so the AAD puts full toenail regrowth at 12 to 18 months and the NHS says up to 18 months after an injury. That slow pace is also why treating a toenail problem, such as fungus, continues long after the infection itself clears.

en.q: How fast do nails grow in a month?
en.a: Fingernails average 3.47 mm per month (not quite a millimeter a week) and toenails 1.62 mm per month, based on a University of North Carolina study of 22 healthy young adults. Rates vary by digit: the little fingernail grew measurably slower than the other fingernails, while the great toenail outpaced the other toes. Younger age and male sex were linked to slightly faster growth, but the differences were not statistically significant.

en.q: Can you make your nails grow faster?
en.a: No measured factor meaningfully speeds up the nail matrix — even nail biting, which was associated with faster growth in the UNC study, fell short of statistical significance. What you can do is prevent slowdowns: the AAD warns that fever, injury, chemotherapy, and major stress can slow or stop growth, and Cleveland Clinic lists conditions like diabetes, hypothyroidism, and zinc deficiency as interruptions. If your nails slow or stop growing with no explanation, the AAD advises seeing a dermatologist.

en.q: How long does it take for paint to dry?
en.a: Latex and acrylic paint are dry to the touch in about 1 to 2 hours, while oil-based paint takes 6 to 8 hours — and Benjamin Moore puts oil-based drying as high as 8 to 16 hours. Dry to the touch is only the first milestone, not a signal to wash or bump the walls. Temperature, humidity, and airflow can stretch or shrink all of these times.

en.q: How long should paint dry between coats?
en.a: Glidden's guidance is 4 hours between coats for latex paint and 24 hours for oil-based paint. Confirm the first coat is dry to the touch, then follow the recoat time printed on the back of your specific can, because manufacturers test each formula individually. Recoating too soon makes the dry time considerably longer and can leave a gloppy, streaky finish.

en.q: How long does it take paint to fully cure?
en.a: Full cure — when paint reaches optimum performance — takes two to three weeks for latex and acrylic paints and 5 to 15 days for oil-based coatings; aerosol finishes cure in up to 48 hours. Sherwin-Williams and Benjamin Moore both define cure as the point of optimum performance, and paint cannot cure until it is dry. Hold off on scrubbing or washing until the cure window is complete.

en.q: At what temperature should you not paint?
en.a: Benjamin Moore calls 77F optimal with an acceptable range of 35-100F, but traditional latex should not be applied below 50F and needs temperatures above 60F to cure properly, because the latex particles must coalesce into a film. Specialty Sherwin-Williams exterior products such as Duration, Resilience, and SuperPaint are formulated for application down to 35F. Above 100F the film can dry before it properly adheres, so avoid both extremes.

en.q: How long does it take for caulk to dry before painting?
en.a: If it is acrylic latex caulk, about 30 minutes: DAP says Alex Plus can be painted within just 30 minutes using either latex or oil-based paints. 100% silicone is never paintable — Gorilla and GE both list their silicone sealants as non-paintable — so paint the surface first and apply the silicone afterward.

en.q: How long after caulking can you shower?
en.a: It depends on the formula. Fast-cure silicones such as GE Advanced Silicone 2 Kitchen & Bath and Gorilla 100% Silicone are water-ready in 30 minutes, DAP's Kwik Seal Ultra tolerates water in about 4 hours, and DAP's conventional kitchen-and-bath silicone needs 12 hours. If your label does not specify, waiting 24 hours is the safe default.

en.q: How long does it take for silicone caulk to fully cure?
en.a: Plan on 24 hours, or 24 to 48 hours in tougher conditions. GE's FAQ says its silicone is water-resistant in as little as 30 minutes but cures within 24 hours, while the GE Silicone 2 specification lists full cure at 24 to 48 hours. Cold air, dry air, and thick beads all push the cure toward the longer end.

en.q: Why is my caulk still tacky after 48 hours?
en.a: Usually the conditions, not the tube. Silicone needs moisture in the air to cure, so cold or very dry air slows it dramatically, and a bead laid too thick cures from the outside in and can stay soft deep inside. Warm the room, give it another day, and test a corner before digging the bead out; soft latex caulk simply needs more time, warmth, and airflow to release its water.

en.q: How long does it take for concrete to cure before you can walk on it?
en.a: Concrete is solid enough to walk on without leaving footprints 24 to 48 hours after pouring. Keep all wheeled traffic — cars, bicycles, skateboards — off the surface, and rope the area off so nobody wanders on early. The slab is far from cured at this point; it will keep gaining strength for weeks.

en.q: How long should concrete cure before I can drive or park a car on it?
en.a: Wait 7 to 10 days before parking a car on a new slab. By then the concrete has cured to at least 70% of its full strength and can support a car and heavy furniture. Very heavy vehicles such as garbage trucks and moving vans should stay off until the full 28 days.

en.q: Is concrete fully cured at 28 days?
en.a: At 28 days concrete reaches the compressive strength it was designed for — 28 days is the standard industry age for testing strength. But the curing reaction never truly stops: concrete continues to harden and gain strength over time, with most of that gain happening in the first few weeks after placement.

en.q: How long should I keep new concrete wet?
en.a: QUIKRETE recommends moist curing for 5 days in warm weather of 70°F or higher, extended to 7 days in cooler weather between 50°F and 70°F. It pays off — the Concrete Network reports that concrete moist-cured for 7 days is about 50% stronger than concrete left uncured. If running a sprinkler all week is impractical, wet burlap, plastic sheeting or a spray-on curing compound are proper alternatives.

en.q: How long does it take acrylic paint to dry to the touch?
en.a: Most thin acrylic films are dry to the touch in 10–30 minutes: Liquitex cites 10–12 minutes for thin applications, Winsor & Newton Galeria dries in 10–20 minutes, and Winsor & Newton Professional in 20–30 minutes. Very thin washes can feel dry within seconds, while thicker films can take an hour or two. Slow-drying lines like Golden OPEN sit at the other extreme and can take a full day to become touch-dry.

en.q: How long does acrylic paint take to fully dry or cure?
en.a: Even after the surface feels dry, the entire thickness of the film needs a few days to dry thoroughly — and that is for very thin films. Paint applied a quarter inch thick or more takes months and even years to be completely dry. Cure is also temperature-dependent: Golden gives an ideal drying range of 70–90°F, and below 49°F (9°C) the polymer solids will not properly coalesce into a continuous film.

en.q: How long should acrylic paint dry before varnishing?
en.a: Wait a day or two on thin paintings, and a week or two where the paint is thick or impasto, before applying an isolation coat. Let the isolation coat dry a minimum of one day before varnishing, and leave at least 4–6 hours between varnish coats — overnight is better. If you plan to oil paint over gesso, Golden calls for a minimum of three days of drying first.

en.q: How do I make acrylic paint dry slower?
en.a: Mist your palette and painting surface with water or use a stay-wet palette, and mix in a slow-dry medium such as Liquitex Slow-Dri, which extends open time by about 40%. Switching to a slow-drying line like Golden OPEN, which can take a full day just to become touch-dry, buys even more blending time. Keep the studio around 70–85°F with humidity under 75%, which Golden describes as ideal for drying.

en.q: How long does oil paint take to dry to the touch?
en.a: A thin film of conventional oil paint is touch-dry in two to 12 days. Fast-drying pigments like raw umber, Prussian blue, raw sienna and cobalt blues get there in about two days, medium colors like ultramarine, ochres and cadmiums in about five, and slow ones like titanium white take more than five. Paint thickness and room temperature also affect these times.

en.q: How can I make oil paint dry faster?
en.a: Mix your paint with an alkyd medium such as Liquin Original — Winsor & Newton says it increases the drying rate by approximately 50 percent, and paintings mixed with it dry in less than 24 hours. Alkyd paints like Griffin are touch-dry in 18 to 24 hours and stay mixable with conventional oils. Also dry your work in daylight: in Golden's tests, darkness stretched some colors' drying times by a factor of three or more.

en.q: How long should you wait before varnishing an oil painting?
en.a: Winsor & Newton recommends waiting at least six months before applying a traditional final varnish such as dammar. Test readiness by rubbing a cotton bud dampened with Sansodor on an inconspicuous area — if no color transfers, you can varnish. Modern mild-solvent varnishes like Gamvar can go on much sooner: once the painting is dry to the touch and firm in its thickest areas, roughly two to three weeks for thin paintings and one to two months for thick ones.

en.q: Why does oil paint take so long to dry?
en.a: Oil paint dries by oxidization — the oil reacts with oxygen in the air — rather than by evaporation, so nothing escapes the film the way water leaves acrylics. Oxygen works inward from the surface, which is why thick impasto passages take a month or two to firm through while thin layers dry in days. Pigment chemistry matters too: some pigments contain cobalt, manganese or copper that act as driers, while others slow the oil down.

en.q: How many miles do tires last on average?
en.a: For a typical driver, tread wears out in three to four years, which works out to roughly 36,000 to 60,000 miles at 12,000 to 15,000 miles a year, according to Edmunds. The realistic range depends on the tire you buy: Michelin's mileage warranties run from 20,000 miles on performance summer tires to 80,000 miles on long-wearing all-season models like the Defender2.

en.q: Do tires go bad after 6 years?
en.a: They can. NHTSA reports that some vehicle and tire manufacturers recommend replacing tires at six to 10 years old regardless of treadwear, and automakers including Ford, Nissan, and Mercedes-Benz advise replacement six years after production. Michelin sets an absolute ceiling of 10 years from the date of manufacture, and that rule includes the spare tire.

en.q: How do I know when my tires need to be replaced?
en.a: Replace any tire whose tread is worn down to 2/32 of an inch — level with the built-in wear bars — even if it is still young. Do the penny test: place a penny upside down in the groove, and if you can see the top of Lincoln's head, the tread is done. Also check the four-digit DOT date code on the sidewall; once a tire passes five years old, Michelin says a specialist should inspect it at least annually.

en.q: What makes tires wear out faster?
en.a: Underinflation is the biggest one: NHTSA says properly inflated tires last an average of 4,700 miles longer, yet only 19 percent of drivers keep their tires correctly inflated. Skipping rotations, poor alignment, potholes, overloading, and aggressive driving all grind tread away sooner. Heat and sun matter too — NHTSA warns tire aging is a greater concern in the southern Sun Belt states, and Edmunds notes coastal climates speed aging as well.

en.q: How long does it take to charge a Tesla at a Supercharger?
en.a: A typical road-trip session from about 10% to 80% takes roughly 15 to 30 minutes. Tesla's official figures are up to 200 miles added in 15 minutes on a Model S, 175 miles on Models 3 and X, and 162 miles on a Model Y. Charging slows sharply past 80%, so most long-distance drivers unplug there.

en.q: How long does it take to charge a Tesla at home on 240V?
en.a: EPA records for the 2025 model year list 9.7 to 14.0 hours at 240 volts from empty to full across the Model 3, Model Y, Model S and Model X. In practice you plug in overnight: Tesla's Wall Connector adds up to 44 miles of range per hour, and the Department of Energy notes Level 2 equipment can charge a typical EV battery overnight.

en.q: How long does it take to charge a Tesla on a regular 120V outlet?
en.a: Tesla says a standard 120-volt household outlet supplies 2 to 3 miles of range per hour, so an empty-to-full charge takes days — roughly five to seven days for a Model 3 Long Range. Tesla notes that if you charge overnight and drive less than 30 to 40 miles per day, a regular outlet can still cover your daily needs.

en.q: Why do Tesla drivers stop charging at 80%?
en.a: Charging speeds slow as the battery fills, and Tesla says reaching 100% will typically take significantly longer than reaching 80%. At high-use Superchargers, Tesla may automatically set your charge limit to 80% to reduce congestion, and congestion fees accrue at busy sites once your battery is at or above 80% — waived only for the first five minutes.

en.q: How long does it take to charge an EV at home?
en.a: On a 240-volt Level 2 home charger, fully recharging a typical battery pack takes 3 to 12 hours — an overnight session, according to fueleconomy.gov. A standard 7.2 kW residential unit adds about 25 miles of range per hour. On the plain 120-volt cord that comes with the car, expect roughly 5 miles per hour, so a full charge from empty takes 20 hours or more.

en.q: How long does it take to charge an EV on a DC fast charger?
en.a: A DC fast charger adds about 100 to 200+ miles of range per 30 minutes, and even a fast charge to 80% capacity can take 30 minutes, per fueleconomy.gov. The quickest sessions finish in less than 20 minutes, according to the AFDC. Charging slows sharply past 80%, so most road-trip drivers unplug around that mark.

en.q: Can you charge an electric car from a regular 120V household outlet?
en.a: Yes. All commercially available EVs in the United States can charge on both Level 1 (a standard 120 V outlet) and Level 2 equipment, according to the AFDC. Level 1 adds only about 5 miles of range per hour — 8 hours gives roughly 40 miles — so it works as a backup, but fully charging a long-range EV from empty takes 20 hours or more.

en.q: Why does EV charging slow down after 80%?
en.a: Charge rate depends on the battery's state of charge, fueleconomy.gov notes — as a lithium-ion pack fills, it resists current. To limit heat and cell stress, the car's battery management system deliberately dials down the charge rate through that upper zone. That is why fast-charging times are quoted to 80% and why the final 20% takes far longer than the run up to it.

en.q: How long is Hamilton the musical?
en.a: Hamilton runs 2 hours and 45 minutes, including one 15-minute intermission. That official figure is the same on Broadway at the Richard Rodgers Theatre, on the North American tour, and in London's West End, so plan on being in the theatre for roughly three hours.

en.q: How long is Hamilton on Disney+?
en.a: The filmed version on Disney+ runs 160 minutes, or 2 hours 40. It was recorded over three live performances in June 2016 with the original principal cast, and its only break is a one-minute intermission card, so it plays slightly differently from the 2h 45m stage show.

en.q: How long is each act of Hamilton?
en.a: The producers publish only a total running time — 2 hours 45 minutes with a 15-minute intermission — not per-act timings, so exact Act One and Act Two lengths are unofficial stopwatch figures. Officially, you get about two and a half hours of stage time, with Act One ending on "Non-Stop" and Act Two opening with "What'd I Miss."

en.q: What time does Hamilton end?
en.a: With a typical 8:00 PM curtain, Hamilton ends around 10:45 PM; a 2:00 PM matinee wraps near 4:45 PM. Add a few minutes of cushion for a hyped crowd or a late curtain hold before you book dinner or a train.

en.q: How long is the average concert?
en.a: A headline set usually runs 75 minutes to about two and a half hours, with arena and stadium headliners around the two-hour mark — Oasis opened their Live '25 tour with a two-hour-plus, 23-song set in Cardiff. Add one or two openers and 35–70 minute changeovers, and the whole night from doors to encore typically lasts around three hours. Marathon acts go longer: Taylor Swift's Eras Tour typically ran 3 hours 15 minutes across 44–46 songs.

en.q: How long do festival sets last?
en.a: Festival slots are set by the running order, not the artist. Small-stage newcomers get about 30–45 minutes, main-stage support acts 45–60 minutes, and headliners 75–90 minutes — at Coachella 2024, Lana Del Rey played 11:20 p.m.–12:50 a.m. and Tyler, The Creator played 11:40 p.m.–12:55 a.m. The festival day itself is the real commitment, with music running from mid-afternoon until as late as 1 a.m. in the tents.

en.q: What time do concerts usually end?
en.a: Most arena and stadium shows finish between about 10:30 and 11 p.m., because large venues enforce curfews written into their licences. When Madonna's Celebration Tour overran the O2's 10:30 p.m. curfew, the show still ended around 11 p.m. and reportedly risked a fine of £10,000 per minute. So if a show starts late at a curfew venue, expect a shortened set or a trimmed encore rather than a later finish.

en.q: How long is a concert with an opening act?
en.a: Plan on the headliner's set plus roughly 45–60 minutes per opener, plus a 35–70 minute changeover between acts. One opener typically turns a two-hour headline set into a three-hour night out. Two openers — like Cast and Richard Ashcroft before Oasis in Cardiff — can push the evening well past three hours from doors to encore.

en.q: How long is the average movie?
en.a: Across every film released worldwide in 2024, the average runtime was 103.6 minutes. The average wide U.S. theatrical release in the 2020s runs about 114 minutes, so a typical movie lands between roughly 100 and 115 minutes — just under two hours. Blockbusters sit well above that: films budgeted over $100 million average about 130 minutes.

en.q: Does a movie's runtime include the credits?
en.a: Yes — every advertised runtime includes the full end credits. The median credit roll is 4 minutes 26 seconds across films from 1920 to 2025, rising to a median of 5 minutes 43 seconds in the 2020s, and superhero films run about 7 minutes 9 seconds of credits. That means a listed 150-minute blockbuster typically contains only about 143 minutes of story.

en.q: Why are blockbuster movies so long now?
en.a: Theaters now compete with streaming by selling big-screen "event" experiences, and longer films justify premium IMAX ticket prices even though they mean fewer showtimes per screen per day. Binge-watching has normalized long runtimes, and as mid-budget dramas moved to streamers, directors like Christopher Nolan and Denis Villeneuve gained the leverage to go long. Films budgeted over $100 million now average about 130 minutes, and the top ten box office films of 2022 averaged 141.

en.q: How long should I plan for a movie at the theater?
en.a: Assume about two hours for a standard release, closer to two and a half hours for a franchise or action title, and three or more for epics like Killers of the Flower Moon (206 minutes) or Avatar: The Way of Water (192 minutes). Add time for previews and concessions — for a blockbuster, block out about three hours end to end. Remember the listed runtime includes the credits, which run 5 to 8 minutes on most big films.

en.q: How long is the average Broadway show?
en.a: Most Broadway shows run between 90 minutes and three hours, including a 15 to 20 minute intermission. Most musicals run about two and a half hours, and the big blockbusters cluster tightly at 2 hours 30 minutes to 2 hours 45 minutes. Plays vary more, from 90-minute one-acts with no intermission to epics like Harry Potter and the Cursed Child at 2 hours 55 minutes.

en.q: How long is a Broadway show with no intermission?
en.a: The hit no-intermission shows are short: SIX and Oh, Mary! each run just 80 minutes straight through. Broadway producer Ken Davenport's analysis of three decades of data found a 20 percentage point rise in the share of one-act shows, and he predicted the "90 minutes no intermission" format will keep spreading. An 80-minute show gets you out roughly two hours earlier than a full-length musical.

en.q: What time does a Broadway show start and end?
en.a: Evening performances typically begin at 7:00, 7:30, or 8:00 PM, and matinees start at 2:00 PM or 3:00 PM. Add the published running time to the curtain time: an 8:00 PM musical with a 2 hour 45 minute runtime, like Wicked or Hamilton, ends around 10:45 PM. A 2:00 PM matinee of a 2 hour 30 minute show ends around 4:30 PM.

en.q: How long is the intermission at a Broadway show?
en.a: Broadway intermissions typically run 15 to 20 minutes and arrive about an hour into the show. Wicked's official FAQ, for example, lists the show as 2 hours 45 minutes including one 15-minute intermission. Full-length musicals almost always take exactly one intermission, while short shows and many newer plays skip it entirely.

en.q: How long do AirPods last on a single charge?
en.a: It depends on the model: AirPods 2 and AirPods 4 are rated for up to 5 hours of listening, AirPods 3 and AirPods Pro 2 for up to 6 hours, and AirPods Pro 3 for up to 8 hours with noise cancellation on. The AirPods 4 with ANC drops to about 4 hours per charge with noise control on, while AirPods Max headphones last up to 20 hours. Independent testing often runs a bit longer than Apple's rated figures.

en.q: How many years do AirPods last before the battery dies?
en.a: Expect about two to three years of daily use, or 300 to 500 charge cycles, before the small lithium-ion cells wear out noticeably, according to SoundGuys. Every charge cycle permanently shaves a little capacity off the batteries, so sessions keep getting shorter. Apple's warranty does not cover batteries that wear down from normal use.

en.q: How long do AirPods last with the charging case?
en.a: Counting the extra charges stored in the case, Apple rates total listening time at up to 30 hours for AirPods 4, AirPods 3 (MagSafe case), and AirPods Pro 2, up to 24 hours with ANC for AirPods Pro 3, and more than 24 hours for AirPods 2. AirPods Max have no case battery. On newer models, five minutes in the case adds around an hour of listening.

en.q: Can you get the battery in AirPods replaced?
en.a: The batteries are not user-replaceable, but Apple offers out-of-warranty battery service: an estimated $49 per set for AirPods 4 and AirPods Pro 2, and $79 for AirPods Max. Apple inspects the device to confirm the final fee, which may be subject to tax, and a shipping fee may be added. Many owners weigh that cost against buying a newer pair with longer per-charge runtime.

en.q: How long does it take for AirPods to fully charge?
en.a: Independent timing measurements put AirPods 1 and 2 at about 25 to 30 minutes from empty to full in the case, AirPods 3, 4, and Pro 2 at 45 to 60 minutes, and AirPods Pro 3 at 30 to 45 minutes. AirPods Max take about 2 hours over USB-C. Apple does not publish 0-to-100% times, so these come from independent tests that line up with Apple's official fast-charge specs.

en.q: How long does the AirPods charging case take to charge?
en.a: The case refills in about 1 to 2 hours over a USB-C or Lightning cable, 2 to 2.5 hours on a MagSafe, Apple Watch, or Qi charger, and 2.5 to 3 hours on a basic 5W wireless pad. Charging with the earbuds inside adds roughly 15 to 30 minutes because the system charges the earbuds first.

en.q: How much listening time do you get from a 5-minute AirPods charge?
en.a: On AirPods 3, AirPods 4, AirPods 4 with ANC, AirPods Pro 2, and AirPods Pro 3, five minutes in the case provides around 1 hour of listening time, per Apple's official specs. AirPods Max get around 1.5 hours from a 5-minute charge, while AirPods 2 need 15 minutes for up to 3 hours of playback.

en.q: Why do my AirPods Pro 3 stop charging before they reach 100%?
en.a: AirPods Pro 3 ship with Optimized Charge Limit on by default. It learns your daily routine and holds the battery at an optimized limit below a full charge when it predicts you will not need one, which preserves battery lifespan. If you genuinely need 100 percent, you can turn it off for just a day in Settings under your AirPods' Battery options.

en.q: How many hours does an iPhone battery last on one charge?
en.a: Apple rates models released since 2024 at 22 to 39 hours of stored video playback: the current lineup spans 26 hours (iPhone 17e) to 39 hours (iPhone 17 Pro Max), with streaming cutting 3 to 5 hours off each rating. Real-world mixed use lands below these lab numbers, which is why most owners still charge overnight.

en.q: How long does an iPhone battery last before it needs to be replaced?
en.a: Apple designs iPhone 15 batteries to retain 80 percent of their original capacity at 1,000 complete charge cycles, and iPhone 14-or-earlier batteries to reach the same threshold at 500 cycles. At one full cycle a day that is roughly two to three years; lighter use stretches it considerably longer. Watch the Battery Health screen and replace the battery when iOS recommends service.

en.q: Why is my iPhone battery draining so fast?
en.a: Apple says the way you use the device has the biggest effect: video and gaming drain fastest, streaming costs 3 to 5 hours versus stored playback, and weak cellular signal makes the radio work harder. Heat permanently reduces capacity, and a chemically aged battery simply holds less charge than a new one. The Battery screen in Settings shows which apps are consuming the power.

en.q: How do I make my iPhone battery last longer?
en.a: For more hours per charge, download video instead of streaming, favor audio, fast-charge to 50 percent when needed, and keep the phone out of hot cars and direct sun. For more years, avoid charging in hot environments, and store a spare device at about 50 percent charge, powered down, somewhere below 90° F (32° C), recharging it to 50 percent every six months if it sits longer than that. Replace the battery based on the Battery Health reading, not a fixed age.

en.q: How long does a Nintendo Switch take to fully charge?
en.a: Approximately 3 hours when the console is powered off or in sleep mode, according to Nintendo's official support documentation. The same estimate applies to the standard Switch, the Switch OLED, the Switch Lite, and the Nintendo Switch 2. Nintendo notes that charging takes longer if the console is in use while plugged in.

en.q: Can I play my Nintendo Switch while it charges?
en.a: Yes. Docked play is charging by design on the standard and OLED models, and in handheld mode you can plug the AC adapter into the console's bottom USB-C port and keep playing. Just expect a slower charge: Nintendo officially states that charging time is longer while the console is in use, so sleep mode or powering off is the fastest way to charge.

en.q: How long do Joy-Con controllers take to charge?
en.a: Approximately 3.5 hours when attached to the charging console or Joy-Con grip, according to Nintendo's Joy-Con FAQ. A full charge delivers up to 20 hours of use, though Nintendo says actual runtime varies with the software and how the controllers are used.

en.q: Why is my Switch taking longer than 3 hours to charge?
en.a: Nintendo's 3-hour estimate assumes the console is off or in sleep mode, so playing while charging is the most common cause. A weak or unofficial USB-C power source also stretches the wait, since Nintendo's figure is stated for its own adapter and dock. Battery age matters too: after about 800 charge cycles, Nintendo says the battery holds about 80 percent of a new console's charge.

en.q: How long do hard-boiled eggs last in the fridge?
en.a: Up to 1 week (7 days) in the refrigerator at 40°F (4°C) or below, according to the USDA FSIS egg storage chart. The clock starts when the eggs finish cooking, not when you peel them, and FSIS says to get them into the fridge within 2 hours of cooking. Store them unpeeled and label the cook date so day 7 does not sneak up on you.

en.q: Do hard-boiled eggs last longer in the shell or peeled?
en.a: In the shell, by a wide margin. Unpeeled hard-boiled eggs keep safely for up to one week, while the American Egg Board says peeled eggs should be eaten the same day. The shell protects the cooked egg from moisture loss, odors, and bacteria, so peel each egg only right before you eat it.

en.q: How long can hard-boiled eggs sit out at room temperature?
en.a: No more than 2 hours, and just 1 hour if the room is above 90°F (32°C), per USDA FSIS. Between 40°F and 140°F — the Danger Zone — bacteria can double in number in as little as 20 minutes. Both FSIS and the American Egg Board say eggs left out of refrigeration longer than 2 hours should be discarded.

en.q: Can you freeze hard-boiled eggs?
en.a: Not whole. The USDA storage chart's freezer column for hard-cooked eggs reads do not freeze, and the American Egg Board explains that whole eggs and whites turn tough and watery when frozen. The one exception is hard-boiled yolks, which can be frozen for toppings or garnishes after a brief hot-water treatment. Extra raw eggs freeze better out of the shell, with yolks and whites beaten together.

en.q: How long do eggs last in the fridge?
en.a: Raw eggs in the shell keep 3 to 5 weeks in the refrigerator at 40 degrees F or below, according to USDA FSIS. The window usually outlasts the sell-by date, which is a store inventory tool, not a safety date. Raw whites or yolks out of the shell last only 2 to 4 days refrigerated.

en.q: Are eggs still good after the sell-by date?
en.a: Usually, yes. On USDA-graded eggs, sell-by style expiration dates can fall no more than 30 days after packing and are not safety dates, and FSIS says a product is still safe and wholesome if handled properly until spoilage is evident. The American Egg Board counts quality for up to 12 weeks past the pack date. When in doubt, crack the egg into a bowl and check for an off-odor or unusual appearance.

en.q: Does the float test tell you if an egg is bad?
en.a: No — it signals age, not safety. FSIS says a floating egg has an enlarged air cell, is of poor quality, but may be perfectly safe to use. A sinking egg can still carry Salmonella, so FSIS recommends cracking into a bowl and checking for an off-odor or unusual appearance, then cooking eggs until the white and yolk are firm.

en.q: Can you freeze raw eggs?
en.a: Yes, but never in the shell. Beat whole eggs just until blended (or separate whites and yolks) into freezer containers and freeze for up to one year; yolks need 1/8 teaspoon of salt or 1 1/2 teaspoons of sugar or corn syrup per 1/4 cup of yolks to stay usable. Thaw overnight in the refrigerator or under cold running water, and use thawed eggs only in thoroughly cooked dishes.

en.q: How long does cooked chicken last in the fridge?
en.a: Cooked chicken lasts 3 to 4 days in the refrigerator at 40°F (4°C) or below, according to USDA FSIS. The window is the same whether the chicken was grilled, roasted, baked, shredded, fried, or from a store rotisserie. Refrigerate it within 2 hours of cooking, and discard anything still in the fridge after day four.

en.q: Can I eat cooked chicken after 5 days in the fridge?
en.a: No. Five days puts cooked chicken past the USDA's 3-to-4-day storage window, so it should be discarded even if it looks and smells fine. USDA rules are based on time and temperature, not appearance, because bacteria such as Salmonella and Campylobacter can reach dangerous levels without changing how the chicken looks.

en.q: How can you tell if cooked chicken has gone bad?
en.a: Rely on the clock, not your nose: USDA rules include no smell test, so discard cooked chicken refrigerated more than 4 days, or left out longer than 2 hours (1 hour if it was above 90°F/32°C). Visible mold or a sour, rotten odor is an obvious toss signal, but the absence of odor means nothing. Reheating to 165°F (74°C) does not rescue chicken that sat out too long.

en.q: Can you freeze cooked chicken?
en.a: Yes. USDA FSIS gives frozen cooked chicken 4 months at 0°F (-18°C) for best quality — casseroles keep 4 to 6 months, chicken broth or gravy 2 to 3 months — and frozen food remains safe indefinitely. Thaw it in the refrigerator, use it within 3 to 4 days or refreeze it, and reheat to 165°F (74°C) measured with a food thermometer.

en.q: How long does cooked rice last in the fridge?
en.a: Cooked rice keeps for 3 to 4 days in the refrigerator at 40°F (4°C) or below, per USDA FSIS guidance — the same window that applies to all cooked leftovers. FSIS's storage chart applies the figure to rice directly: dry rice holds 2 years on the shelf, and "after cooking, 3 to 4 days in the refrigerator." Get it into the fridge within 2 hours of cooking (1 hour if the room is above 90°F) and the full window is yours.

en.q: Is cooked rice still safe after 5 days in the fridge?
